note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
Did it change after Joseph’s table? No. When his family came down, Joseph told them what to say to Pharaoh. “the men are shepherds, for their trade hath been to feed cattle;” and when Pharaoh asks, “What is your occupation?” they were to answer: “Thy servants’ trade hath been about cattle from our youth even until now, both we, and also our fathers: that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians.”

The Israelites were known as shepherds. Because of the war with the shepherd kings before Joseph arrived, the Egyptians hated shepherds, so the Israelites were despised twice over, as Hebrews and as shepherds.

So Israel was placed in Goshen, an isolated area away from the Egyptians. Egyptians and shepherds could not live in the same vicinity, which means there were no Egyptians living among us to put their blood into ours. That is segregation; that is redlining. It is nothing new.

That separation is the ground Exodus 1 grows out of. A people set apart, more and mightier than their masters, “dealt wisely” with: taskmasters over them, building Pithom and Raamses, serving “with rigour” in mortar, brick and “all manner of service in the field.” The same pattern followed us into America: set apart, built the Capitol and the White House, worked the fields.

points: Jacob rose up from Beersheba, and his sons carried him and their little ones and their wives in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent, and all his seed came with him into Egypt.
All the souls of the house of Jacob which came into Egypt were threescore and ten: 70 souls.
Joseph fell on his father's neck, and wept on his neck a good while. And Israel said, now let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou art yet alive.

Joseph instructed them: when Pharaoh shall ask, what is your occupation, ye shall say, thy servants' trade hath been about cattle from our youth; for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians. Joseph was fully aware of the history of the Hyksos, the shepherd kings from Palestine who had taken over the Delta and ruled Egypt in the 15th Dynasty. That's why he told his father and brothers to tell Pharaoh they were shepherds, so they would be placed apart in Goshen.
All the souls of the house of Jacob which came into Egypt were threescore and ten. A score is twenty, so three score is sixty, and ten more makes seventy souls.

points: Naming their trade set Israel apart in Goshen, which was fertile land, and the favor Joseph had was bestowed upon him through Pharaoh to give them that land.

points: Joseph instructed his brethren to tell Pharaoh their trade hath been about cattle from their youth, both they and also their fathers, that they might dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians.

There is history behind that instruction. Somewhere between the fifteenth and seventeenth dynasties Egypt was ruled by the Hyksos, called the shepherd kings, a group of Canaanites or Hittites that occupied the land; the Egyptians did not deal with shepherds.
